subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core durable conversational-rule layer and cross-channel explicit multi-mention reply contract, or keep this as memory-plugin/channel-plugin policy plus narrower Feishu fixes?
rationale: The requested behavior changes durable memory authority, workspace-rule precedence, session state, and channel delivery semantics; code inspection shows partial mechanisms exist, but no current owner-approved product contract says how they should compose.

options.title: Keep Open For Product Design
options.body: Define the durable rule authority model, conflict/supersession rules, storage/migration boundary, and explicit multi-mention contract before implementation.

options.title: Split Narrow Feishu Work
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72504 and related Feishu PRs for the parser/message-loss bug while keeping durable rule learning as a separate design item.

options.title: Route Durable Learning To Plugins
options.body: Decide that rule learning belongs in a memory or bundle-style plugin unless a missing core/plugin API is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Product Design
recommendation.body: Define the durable rule authority model, conflict/supersession rules, storage/migration boundary, and explicit multi-mention contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The durable-rule portion most closely intersects the memory-core promotion system that this owner introduced, with Feishu owners still needed for channel semantics.
